title: Rigveda 10.134: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.134: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.134 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 122v-123v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.134.1-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 123r
translation.original_text:
1u̱bhe yad i̍ndra̱ roda̍sī āpa̱prātho̱ṣā i̍va | ma̱hānta̍ṁ tvā ma̱hīnā̍ṁ sa̱mrāja̍ṁ carṣaṇī̱nāṁ de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
2ava̍ sma durhaṇāya̱to marta̍sya tanuhi sthi̱ram | a̱dha̱spa̱daṁ tam ī̍ṁ kṛdhi̱ yo a̱smām̐ ā̱dide̍śati de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
3ava̱ tyā bṛ̍ha̱tīr iṣo̍ vi̱śvaśca̍ndrā amitrahan | śacī̍bhiḥ śakra dhūnu̱hīndra̱ viśvā̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍r de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
4ava̱ yat tvaṁ śa̍takrata̱v indra̱ viśvā̍ni dhūnu̱ṣe | ra̱yiṁ na su̍nva̱te sacā̍ saha̱sriṇī̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍r de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
5ava̱ svedā̍ ivā̱bhito̱ viṣva̍k patantu di̱dyava̍ḥ | dūrvā̍yā iva̱ tanta̍vo̱ vy a1̱̍smad e̍tu durma̱tir de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
translation.text:
1As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven. So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
2Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
3Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies. With all thy powers, O Ṣakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:
4As thou, O Ṣatakratu, thou, O Indra, shakest all things down As wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold.
5Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall. Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 123r (OPenn image 122, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.134.1 ‹-ajījanat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 123v, begins in RV 10.134.6 ‹-padājo vayāṁ yathā yamo›. Verses 10.134.1-5 end on this page; 10.134.1 begins on fol. 122v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.134.6-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 123v
translation.original_text:
6dī̱rghaṁ hy a̍ṅku̱śaṁ ya̍thā̱ śakti̱m bibha̍rṣi mantumaḥ | pūrve̍ṇa maghavan pa̱dājo va̱yāṁ yathā̍ yamo de̱vī jani̍try ajījanad bha̱drā jani̍try ajījanat ||
7naki̍r devā minīmasi̱ naki̱r ā yo̍payāmasi mantra̱śrutya̍ṁ carāmasi | pa̱kṣebhi̍r apika̱kṣebhi̱r atrā̱bhi saṁ ra̍bhāmahe ||
translation.text:
6Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor! As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan.
7Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command. Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 123v (OPenn image 123, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.134.6 ‹-padājo vayāṁ yathā yamo›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 124r, begins in RV 10.135.4 ‹-prāvartata sam ito nāvy›. Verses 10.134.6-7 end on this page; 10.134.6 begins on fol. 123r.
